$doc: Reusable RISER sound-effect catalog (cinematic build-ups / rises used to lead into a reveal, title drop, stat punch, or hard cut). Mirrors assets/music/library.json. All files here are silence-trimmed at the edges (leading dead-air + trailing dead-air removed, conservative -50dB so the soft BUILD is never clipped; internal silence preserved). Raw/untrimmed originals + waveform proofs live in ./_raw/. When editing a video, scan this file and pick by `ends_in_impact` (does it self-resolve on a hit, or do you cut on it / add a separate [IMPACT]?), `duration_sec`, `intensity`, `peak_position`, and `best_for`.
$schema_note: ends_in_impact is the key field: 'built_in_hit' = the SFX contains its own downbeat/boom at the end (no separate [IMPACT] needed); 'climax_cut' = crescendos to a peak then stops, cut the video ON the peak; 'swell_taper' / 'soft_taper' = rises then decays with NO hard hit, use as a transition or add your own [IMPACT] at the cut. intensity is 1-5. peak_position = where the loudest moment lands. LICENSING: Soundstripe SFX have NO Content-ID code (usage-acknowledgement doc only, per Mike) — nothing to paste in a description; Envato Elements = subscription license certificate tied to the item/register; ElevenLabs = AI-generated on Mike's account.

risers.title: DSGN Rise (cinematic suspense, ElevenLabs)
risers.license: AI-generated on Mike's ElevenLabs account (no third-party clearance needed).
risers.shape: deep rumble rising in pitch + heartbeat + high ring, a split-second cut-to-silence, then a deep bass HIT + water splash
risers.texture: cinematic suspense: sub rumble, heartbeat, high-frequency ring, bass drop, water splash
risers.best_for: the BIGGEST reveal / drop — has its own built-in impact, so NO separate [IMPACT] needed; align the video cut to the bass hit at the end. Note the deliberate ~0.25s cut-to-silence right before the hit (kept).
risers.description: Cinematic suspense build with a built-in bass-hit + splash impact.
risers.source_prompt: Create a cinematic suspense sound that builds tension right before a big moment. Start with a low, deep rumble that slowly rises in pitch like a distant engine revving or a cinematic riser. Add a subtle heartbeat and a high-frequency ringing tone that increases in intensity. Right before the impact, everything cuts to silence for a split second, then a deep bass hit followed by a large water splash sound. The feeling should be intense, suspenseful.
